intro: Look for the turquoise: its tiles pick the Green Tomb out from across Bursa. This tomb in Bursa province, dating from 1421, belongs to Mehmed I, and its cenotaph carries the richest tilework of the age.
history: Mehmed I was the sultan who brought the Ottomans out of the interregnum. He died in 1421 and was buried on the slope of the complex he had built for himself in Bursa. His vizier Hacı İvaz Paşa oversaw both the tomb and the Green Mosque opposite. And the turquoise tiles that gave the tomb its name? They were renewed after the earthquake of 1855.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the turquoise tiled façade and the cenotaph of Mehmed I. Then look closely at the tiled mihrab, the carved door and the stucco work.
facts: Did you know? The tiles over the cenotaph were made in the coloured-glaze technique their masters brought from Tabriz, and the masters' signatures can still be read. The turquoise tiling that gives the tomb its name was renewed after the earthquake of 1855, though some of the original tiles survive inside. And the cenotaph of Mehmed I is the most elaborate piece of Ottoman tilework surviving from the Bursa period.
outro: This brings our visit to the Green Tomb to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones and tiles untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Let this turquoise keep shining for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
